The Meals & Beverages segment includes Pepperidge Farm-type snacking products in foodservice and Canada, and Latin America snacking, alongside soup, simple meals and beverages (Campbell's soups, Swanson, Prego, Pace, V8 juices, Rao's, SpaghettiOs, Michael Angelo's frozen entrees). V8 juices/beverages and various discretionary meal products fall within categories exposed to volume/consumption shifts, though the company does not break out any GLP-1-related impact.

Consolidated net sales were $7,607 million for the nine months ended May 3, 2026 (down from $7,932 million prior year) and $2,366 million for the quarter (down from $2,475 million), across the Meals & Beverages and Snacks segments. Sales declines are disclosed but no attribution to the GLP-1 demand shift is made.

The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The scan decides which; a wording that pre-excluded the category would defeat the classifier it is meant to configure.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the sub-structure tag says which side a name sits on — this is deliberate: a single company can be suppressed in one category and helped in another (a nutrition portfolio whose snacking brands face volume decline while its protein brands face a tailwind), and a one-sided driver would mis-grade exactly those names. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. disclosed_facts.fact: Soft pretzels (SUPERPRETZEL, BRAUHAUS, FEDERAL PRETZEL, BAVARIAN BAKERY etc.) accounted for 18% of Company revenue in FY2025 (18% FY2024, 19% FY2023) — a salty/baked snacking category on the suppressed side of the consumption shift.

Frozen novelties (DIPPIN DOTS ice cream, LUIGI'S Italian ice, WHOLE FRUIT bars/sorbet, PHILLY SWIRL, MINUTE MAID juice bars) were 16% of Company revenue in FY2025 (17% FY2024, 17% FY2023) — a sweet frozen-dessert/discretionary snacking category on the suppressed side.

Churros (HOLA! brand deep-fried pastries topped with cinnamon sugar) were 6% of Company sales in FY2025 (7% FY2024, 7% FY2023) — a sweet baked/fried discretionary snack category on the suppressed side.

Bakery products (fig and fruit bars, cookies, breads, rolls, crumb, muffins, donuts under READI-BAKE, COUNTRY HOME, MARY B'S, DADDY RAY'S, HILL & VALLEY) were 27% of Company sales in FY2025 (26% FY2024, 26% FY2023) — the Company's largest category and a baked-goods category on the suppressed side.

Frozen beverages (ICEE frozen carbonated beverage, SLUSH PUPPIE, PARROT ICE — made from water, sweeteners and flavors) were 14% of Company revenue in FY2025 (15% FY2024, 14% FY2023) — a sugared/frozen discretionary beverage category on the suppressed side.
Other products include FUNNEL CAKE FACTORY funnel cakes and handheld products (7% of sales FY2025), further discretionary snack/baked formats on the suppressed side.

primary_business: Manufacturer of snack foods (soft pretzels, frozen novelties, churros, bakery products, handheld snacks) and distributor of frozen beverages (ICEE, SLUSH PUPPIE) to foodservice and retail supermarket channels.

disclosed_facts.fact: The Company operates and franchises Jack in the Box, one of the nation's largest hamburger chains with 2,136 quick-service restaurants across 22 states, offering burgers (Jumbo Jack, Buttery Jack, Smash Jack), breakfast sandwiches, tacos, curly fries, egg rolls, and real ice cream shakes across five day parts including a 'snack' and 'late night' day part. Company restaurant sales of $96.3M and franchise royalties/rental/advertising revenues are all generated from QSR operations.

The Company operates and franchises Del Taco, one of the nation's largest Mexican-American QSR chains with 576 restaurants across 18 states, serving burritos, fries and Mexican/American favorites to approximately two million guests each week; on October 15, 2025 the Company signed a Stock Purchase Agreement to sell Del Taco for $115 million, and Del Taco is reported as discontinued operations.

For the quarter ended July 5, 2026, total revenues from continuing operations (Jack in the Box QSR) were $257.7M (company restaurant sales $96.3M, franchise rental $73.0M, royalties/other $43.1M, advertising contributions $45.3M); Del Taco results are reported in discontinued operations with a year-to-date loss of $20.1M — all QSR-category revenue facing the suppressed-volume side of the shift.

primary_business: Operator and franchisor of quick-service restaurant chains (Jack in the Box hamburger chain, plus Del Taco being divested).
key_unknowns: The filings contain no discussion whatsoever of GLP-1/incretin therapy, weight-loss drugs, or any resulting change in consumer eating volume or food-category demand — exposure to the shift is inferred solely from the company being a QSR operator, not disclosed as a factor.
No disclosed impact of the GLP-1 demand shift on transaction counts, traffic, ticket size, or same-store sales is broken out; the driver is not named in risk factors or MD&A.

The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. disclosed_facts.fact: Weight Management is Herbalife's largest product category at 54.5% of net sales in 2025 (55.4% 2024, 56.3% 2023), comprising meal replacement, protein shakes, drink mixes, weight loss supplements, healthy snacks, and metabolism-boosting teas — representative products include Formula 1 Healthy Meal, Protein Drink Mix, Personalized Protein Powder, Total Control, Prolessa Duo, and Protein Bars.

The Formula 1 Nutritional Shake Mix, the company's best-selling product line (a meal-replacement/protein shake), approximated 25% of net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 — a product-based meal replacement that is two-sided under the driver (competes with incretins as a weight-loss method and supports incretin users as protein/meal-replacement nutrition).

Herbalife describes itself as the number one active and lifestyle nutrition brand in the world and seller of the number one protein shake in the world, providing weight management, targeted nutrition, energy/sports/fitness products across 95 markets — a high-protein, meal-replacement nutrition portfolio.

In 2025 the company introduced MultiBurn in North America as part of its stated mission to lead innovation in metabolic health and weight-loss supplements, and expanded into healthy snacking with Protein Gelato in Brazil — product activity positioned in the metabolic/weight-loss and protein-snacking categories.

The company cites the obesity epidemic and increasing interest in fitness/living healthier as global trends powering its business, and its Weight Management category includes 'healthy snacks' and protein bars — placing some disclosed volume in the snacking category as well as the protein/meal-replacement category.

Total net sales were $2,644.0 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 (up from $2,480.8 million a year earlier), but the interim financials do not break out revenue by product category or by weight-loss method versus incretin-support nutrition.

Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. driver: the GLP-1 DEMAND SHIFT — incretin (GLP-1/GIP) therapy at population scale re-shaping FOOD AND BEVERAGE consumption: users eat materially less by volume and re-weight what they do eat toward protein and satiety, so demand moves AWAY from high-volume discretionary calories and TOWARD protein-dense, portion-controlled and satiety-positioned products. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the sub-structure tag says which side a name sits on — this is deliberate: a single company can be suppressed in one category and helped in another (a nutrition portfolio whose snacking brands face volume decline while its protein brands face a tailwind), and a one-sided driver would mis-grade exactly those names. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The scan decides which; a wording that pre-excluded the category would defeat the classifier it is meant to configure.

Omada recently announced a capability to prescribe GLP-1 therapies and other anti-obesity medications (AOMs), launching later in the year, adding prescribing and medication management from licensed providers. This is a prescribing/dispensing CHANNEL for incretins, which is an explicitly excluded adjacent driver, not exposure to the food-and-beverage consumption shift.

For the three months ended June 30, 2026, total revenue was $87.8 million, split between Services revenue ($80.7 million) and Hardware revenue ($7.1 million from connected devices such as scales and glucose monitors). None of this revenue is attributed to a food or beverage consumption category; it is care-services and connected-device revenue.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the sub-structure tag says which side a name sits on — this is deliberate: a single company can be suppressed in one category and helped in another (a nutrition portfolio whose snacking brands face volume decline while its protein brands face a tailwind), and a one-sided driver would mis-grade exactly those names. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. disclosed_facts.fact: Scholar Rock is a clinical/pre-commercial biopharmaceutical company developing apitegromab, an anti-myostatin monoclonal antibody, for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases. It reports NO product revenue (all filings show only operating losses), and its business is a therapeutic drug, not a food, beverage or nutrition product. This is a pharmaceutical developer, not a participant in the food/beverage consumption categories of the GLP-1 demand shift.

This ties to incretin THERAPY as an adjunct pharmaceutical, not to the food/beverage consumption shift, and is a drug-development/partnering intent, not disclosed revenue in a suppressed or benefiting consumption category.

driver: the GLP-1 DEMAND SHIFT — incretin (GLP-1/GIP) therapy at population scale re-shaping FOOD AND BEVERAGE consumption: users eat materially less by volume and re-weight what they do eat toward protein and satiety, so demand moves AWAY from high-volume discretionary calories and TOWARD protein-dense, portion-controlled and satiety-positioned products. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the sub-structure tag says which side a name sits on — this is deliberate: a single company can be suppressed in one category and helped in another (a nutrition portfolio whose snacking brands face volume decline while its protein brands face a tailwind), and a one-sided driver would mis-grade exactly those names. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The scan decides which; a wording that pre-excluded the category would defeat the classifier it is meant to configure.

The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The scan decides which; a wording that pre-excluded the category would defeat the classifier it is meant to configure.

disclosed_facts.fact: The retail segment's in-store merchandise offering is concentrated in categories that sit on the suppressed-volume side of the GLP-1 shift: 'candy, salty snacks, bakery and packaged sweet snacks,' plus take-home packaged beverages and beer. The company names its 'six core destination merchandise categories' as packaged beverages, candy, salty snacks, packaged sweet snacks, alternative snacks and beer — which represented approximately 54% of same-store merchandise contribution for the year ended December 31, 2025. In-store merchandise gross profit was 52.4% of retail segment gross profit dollars, on approximately $1.5 billion of in-store sales/other revenues. The disclosure does not, however, quantify how much revenue is specifically confectionery/snacking versus other in-store categories, so the driver-category share is not itself broken out.

The company sells fuel and merchandise through convenience stores and operates foodservice/QSR — approximately 965 stores with grab-n-go food, 140 delis (fried chicken, pizza, sandwiches, chicken tenders, potato wedges), and approximately 90 quick-service national-brand restaurants such as Dunkin and Subway — categories (QSR, baked goods, sugared beverages) that sit on the suppressed-volume side. Foodservice/QSR revenue is not broken out and no GLP-1 impact is disclosed.

The Transformation Plan launched the 'fas craves' remodeled food-forward format to elevate the assortment of hot and cold grab-and-go food and dispensed beverages, described as relevant, delicious and affordable — a strategic emphasis on foodservice, but with no disclosure tying the offering to protein-dense/satiety/portion-controlled positioning or to the GLP-1 consumption shift in either direction.

For the two quarters ended June 28, 2026, product sales were $673.1 million out of $698.0 million total net revenues (product sales were $315.7M of $331.0M in Q2 2026), meaning the overwhelming majority of disclosed revenue is generated from selling doughnuts — a sweet baked-good in the suppressed snacking/confectionery category — quantifying the scale of the company's exposure to the suppressed side of the shift.

Among enumerated forward-looking risk factors, the company lists 'negative impacts on our business due to changes in consumer spending habits, consumer preferences, or demographic trends,' but does not name or quantify GLP-1/incretin therapy or its effect on doughnut consumption.

primary_business: Omni-channel maker and retailer of fresh doughnuts (sweet baked goods / confectionery) sold through shops, fresh delivery and digital channels globally.

driver: the GLP-1 DEMAND SHIFT — incretin (GLP-1/GIP) therapy at population scale re-shaping FOOD AND BEVERAGE consumption: users eat materially less by volume and re-weight what they do eat toward protein and satiety, so demand moves AWAY from high-volume discretionary calories and TOWARD protein-dense, portion-controlled and satiety-positioned products. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the sub-structure tag says which side a name sits on — this is deliberate: a single company can be suppressed in one category and helped in another (a nutrition portfolio whose snacking brands face volume decline while its protein brands face a tailwind), and a one-sided driver would mis-grade exactly those names. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The scan decides which; a wording that pre-excluded the category would defeat the classifier it is meant to configure.

driver: the GLP-1 DEMAND SHIFT — incretin (GLP-1/GIP) therapy at population scale re-shaping FOOD AND BEVERAGE consumption: users eat materially less by volume and re-weight what they do eat toward protein and satiety, so demand moves AWAY from high-volume discretionary calories and TOWARD protein-dense, portion-controlled and satiety-positioned products. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE IN SCOPE and the sub-structure tag says which side a name sits on — this is deliberate: a single company can be suppressed in one category and helped in another (a nutrition portfolio whose snacking brands face volume decline while its protein brands face a tailwind), and a one-sided driver would mis-grade exactly those names. The structure is PARALLEL consumption categories, not a supply chain: (1) suppressed volume — sweet and salty snacking, confectionery, baked goods, sugared beverages, quick-service restaurants, alcohol; (2) benefiting nutrition — high-protein foods and shakes, portion-controlled and meal-replacement formats, satiety/fibre positioning, medical and active nutrition; (3) adjacent — distribution, private-label manufacture and delivery INTO either side. Exposure must be to the SHIFT, grounded in disclosed activity — NOT generic packaged-food exposure, NOT the incretin MANUFACTURERS or their supply chain (that is a different driver), NOT the PRESCRIBING AND TELEHEALTH CHANNELS through which incretins are dispensed, and NOT fitness or coaching services. **Product-based meal replacement is IN SCOPE, not excluded** — it is sold as a product and its exposure is genuinely two-sided: as a weight-loss METHOD it competes with incretins and is suppressed, and as nutrition support for incretin users it benefits. The scan decides which; a wording that pre-excluded the category would defeat the classifier it is meant to configure.
